page_notes: Introduction and front matter only; no numbered lexical-entry segments occur on this page. The paper is a supplement to A Dravidian Etymological Dictionary (DED), A Dravidian Etymological Dictionary: Supplement (DEDS), and Dravidian Borrowings from Indo-Aryan (DBIA), containing new etymological groups plus additions and corrections to old groups. The authors identify new material especially from Tulu, Gondi (particularly Koya), Kannada dialects, and the provisionally independent language claimants Betta Kuruba, Belari, and Koraga. Entry numbers follow DED and DEDS. New DED/DEDS entries use the prefix S² followed by a new series beginning with 1. DBIA additions and corrections use DBIA as the prefix for changes to old numbered entries, while new DBIA entries use DBIA S followed by a new series beginning with 1. New material generally retains its source transcription, except that all long vowels are retranscribed with a macron. The source uses Roman and italic type for linguistic entries and their glosses, and places Betta Kuruba between Kannada and Kodagu, with Belari and Koraga after Tulu. The page begins additions to the bibliography and list of sources: Tamil (Ta.)—DED §17, Malayalam (Ma.)—DED §18, and Toda (To.)—DED §20; listed works include Andronov, RS, TPM, Tiyya, and K. M. Narayana Menon. The page also contains acknowledgements and a footnote reference to Emeneau in Current Trends in Linguistics, vol. 5, South Asia, p. 342 (The Hague, 1969).
